lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1664: no phantom syllable

Owner, after I offered to "re-tune" two place names: "there should be no a sound
in front of either of those. the s and the n are the starting sound of each
word. where are you getting an AY sound before that — to me it reads like you're
mispronouncing the word, not a tone or inflection, but adding a syllable."

⚠⚠⚠ HE IS RIGHT, AND MY FRAMING WAS THE PROBLEM. I reported this as a vowel
quality issue — "eh" coming out as "AY" — which invited a better spelling of the
same wrong thing. It is not a vowel problem. The leading token should not be
there at all. Samarran is three syllables and opens on S. Nimari is three and
opens on N. Both have been saying four since OTA-104.

⚠ THE CAUSE IS A MISREAD OF THE PLAYTESTER'S IPA. OTA-104 was handed
/ɛsɛmɔːɾɛn/ and /ɛnɛmɑɹi/, saw the leading ɛ, and promoted it to its own
space-separated token — which this file's own header says espeak treats as a
separate WORD. Then it recorded the mistake as a finding: "all three open with a
leading /ɛ/ schwa that the prior respellings dropped. Samarran and Nimari are
4-syllable words, not 3." Both sentences are false, and the second is exactly
the sort of confident note that stops the next reader from checking. It stopped
me twice tonight — I read that comment during the OTA-1659 audit and moved on.

Measured (`espeak-ng -v en-us -q --ipa`), these were not shades off. They were
different words:

    eh sem or en    → ˈeɪ sˈɛm ɔːɹ ˈɛn    "AY-SEM-OR-EN"   (4 beats, 4 stresses)
    Samarran        → sˈæmæɹən            "SAM-a-run"      ✓
    eh neh mah ree  → ˈeɪ nˈeɪ mˈɑː ɹˈiː  "AY-NAY-MAH-REE" ("neh" also says NAY)
    Nimari          → nˈɪmɚɹi             "NIM-uh-ree"     ✓

⚠⚠ SO THE FIX IS REMOVAL, NOT A RE-TUNE. That is the third time in six OTAs that
the right answer here was to delete an entry rather than re-spell it — "the" and
"doesn't" went the same way in OTA-1659, for the same reason: an override was
added to correct a word the phonemizer already read properly, and the override
was the mispronunciation.

⚠ ASGARDAR STAYS, and the distinction matters. A-s-gardar genuinely opens on a
vowel, so its "ez" is the first syllable of the word rather than a beat welded
in front of it. Same syllable count as the raw word, different vowel — which is
what he asked for at OTA-104. He complained about two names, not three, and he
was precise about which.

⚠⚠ AND THE SUITE NOW GUARDS THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. The defect is not "eh"
— it is a respelling that changes how many beats a word has. ota1664 checks the
chunk count of every surviving entry against the count verified here, so the
next entry that adds or drops a syllable fails a test instead of shipping and
waiting for someone to notice it in a sentence.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green.
